beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Hallo, this is Liam, in for Bear. There is a skill called your-turn that most fellows will look at and think it is a whole workflow. It is not. It is a closing-block skill that standardizes the last three beats of every claude-explainer reel, then hands off. So I asked Claude to read the SKILL dot m-d and tell me what it actually rewrites.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — the anatomy of your-turn: SKILL.md plus one apply_your_turn.py script. Small doctrine, small surface.
beats.narration_text: Every skill on this toolkit is a folder Claude reads before working. Your-turn is one SKILL dot m-d plus one Python script — apply underscore your underscore turn dot p-y. The doctrine lives in the SKILL file. The script is the deterministic transformer that applies it.

beats.role_note: The three-beat block, in order. VERDICT → YOUR TURN → OUTRO. Nothing above, nothing below.
beats.narration_text: Here is the block, in fixed order. Beat one — VERDICT, on the artifact card, opens with the handoff line then the full recap. Beat two — YOUR TURN, on the composer, shows a prompt relevant to this specific video and Liam reads the whole thing aloud. Beat three — the title outro, poster serif, Liam re-reads the reel's own title. Three beats, one voice, always closing.

beats.role_note: Mechanism 1 — The handoff line. Persona-aware: prior body beat was Bear → 'Thanks Bear, let's recap with Claude.'; anything else → 'Let's recap with Claude.' 0.5s lead pause.
beats.narration_text: First decision. The handoff line changes based on who narrated the body. If the previous beat was Bear, the recap opens with — Thanks Bear, let's recap with Claude. If the previous beat was already Liam, it just opens — Let's recap with Claude. There is a half-second lead pause so the handoff breathes. The script reads the prior beat's engine to decide which line to write.

body: two branches — from Bear vs from Liam

props.heading: The handoff knows the persona.
props.body: The handoff wording is decided by the persona of the beat immediately before the verdict. Prior body beat's engine reads elevenlabs (Bear) → 'Thanks Bear, let's recap with Claude.' Anything else (Liam already on the mic) → 'Let's recap with Claude.' Both open with an explicit 0.5s lead pause so the transition breathes.
props.quote: The handoff wording is decided by the persona of the beat immediately before the verdict — persona bear → 'Thanks Bear, let's recap with Claude.'; anything else → 'Let's recap with Claude.'

beats.role_note: Mechanism 2 — drafts.json is the human gate. The prompt (and the recap when the reel lacks a verdict) is DRAFTED per slug, reviewed, then applied.
beats.narration_text: Second decision, and this is the one non-deterministic step. The YOUR TURN prompt must be relevant to the specific reel — so it is drafted per slug into a drafts dot j-son file. One entry per slug — a prompt, and optionally a recap for reels that don't have a verdict card yet. The human reviews drafts dot j-son BEFORE any audio spend or render. This is the one phase gate.

props.heading: drafts.json is the human gate.
props.body: One JSON map, slug → { prompt, recap? }. The prompt is a real question a viewer would paste into Claude after watching — grounded in the reel's own material, ending in a concrete multi-part ask. recap is drafted ONLY for reels that lack a verdict card. Review drafts.json BEFORE any audio spend or render.
props.quote: This is the one non-deterministic step and the one human gate — review drafts.json before applying.
props.cite: your-turn SKILL.md · Auto-drafting the YOUR TURN prompt

beats.role_note: Mechanism 3 — VERDICT card fixes. Enlarged from 860px hard-pin to ~84% width; leading '1.' and '2.' numbers stripped from artifactLines because the card numbers them itself.
beats.narration_text: Third decision, and it fixes two defects in one edit. The verdict card was hard-pinned to eight hundred sixty pixels on a nineteen twenty frame — small, floating, indefensible. It now fills eighty-four percent of the width with legible type. One component edit — every reel bigger on re-render. And the double-numbered recap lines — where authors typed one dot, two dot, and the card also numbered them — those are stripped from artifactLines both when writing and defensively at render.

props.heading: Bigger card. Cleaner lines.
props.body: Two catalog-wide defects, folded into this skill. ClaudeVerdictArtifact.tsx was hard-pinned to 860px on a 1920 frame — now fills ~84% width with legible type. And ~160 recap lines across the catalog had authored '1.' / '2.' prefixes colliding with the card's own numbering — the transformer strips leading numbers, and the component strips them defensively too (stripLeadNum).
props.quote: One component edit fixes every reel on re-render. The transformer strips leading numbers from artifactLines, and the component now strips them defensively too — so it can never happen again.

beats.role_note: Mechanism 4 — YOUR TURN beat: Liam reads the prompt in full. props.command == narration_text.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision, and it is what makes YOUR TURN feel like a real handoff. Liam reads the prompt out loud — the full thing. The narration text and the composer's command field are the same string. Greeting slot reads — Your turn. Full stop. The composer types the prompt while Liam speaks it. No 'here is your prompt' filler. No paraphrase. The prompt IS the narration.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — dry-run demo. Synthetic beat sheet fixture in demo/. Show the report output (changed / skipped / needs_prompt).
beats.narration_text: Now watch it run — on a synthetic fixture in this reel's demo folder. Dry-run only, no real reel is touched. The script scans the sheet, finds the closing YOUR TURN and OUTRO, cleans the verdict, rewrites the three beats, and writes a report. Changed, skipped, needs prompt, errors. Look at the report — one fixture changed, zero errors, and the notes name every edit the transformer made.

props.body: Ran apply_your_turn.py --dry-run against a synthetic beat sheet in this reel's demo/. Report: changed=1, skipped=0, needs_prompt=0, errors=0. props.quote: The transformer is idempotent — re-running never stacks handoffs or re-numbers. Sheets without a verdict card (slate cuts, other families) are skipped untouched.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY / documented limitation. What your-turn does NOT do — no body edits, no publish, re-render is a separate human-triggered step.
beats.narration_text: Now what your-turn does NOT do. It never touches the body. It never publishes. Applying the block and even re-rendering the reel is safe — going public is a separate manual step in YouTube Studio. And the re-render itself is human-triggered per reel, because re-uploading replaces the video file via a NEW ID and the old URL and its views are lost. That is why the SKILL says — batch deliberately.

props.heading: What your-turn does NOT do.
props.body: Three limits, all stated in the SKILL. (1) Only edits the closing three beats — the body is out of scope. (2) Never publishes — going public is a manual Studio flip. (3) Re-render + re-upload is a separate human-triggered step per reel, because a new upload replaces the file via a new video ID and the old URL and views are lost. Batch deliberately.
props.quote: Only edits the closing three beats. The body is out of scope. Never publishes — applying the block and re-rendering is safe; going public is a manual Studio flip.

beats.role_note: VERDICT artifact — six lines recapping the split. Bookends inherited; the closing three beats owned; drafts.json is the human gate; and when to reach elsewhere.
beats.narration_text: So the split. Bookends up to the body — INHERITED from ai-explainer. The closing three beats — OWNED. The handoff line is persona-aware. Drafts dot j-son is the human gate before any spend. The verdict card is fixed once, every reel bigger. And reach elsewhere if the sheet has no your-turn or Liam outro — this skill skips it.

artifactLines: Bookends INHERITED — the parent claude-explainer chassis owns everything up to the body.
Closing three beats OWNED — VERDICT → YOUR TURN → OUTRO, in that order, always Liam.
Handoff is PERSONA-AWARE — prior beat was Bear → 'Thanks Bear'; prior was Liam → 'Let's recap.'
drafts.json is the HUMAN GATE — one prompt per slug, reviewed before any audio spend or render.
Verdict card FIXED once — 84% width, leading '1.'/'2.' stripped defensively at write and render.
REACH ELSEWHERE if the sheet has no your-turn or Liam outro — this skill skips it untouched.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready planning prompt. Liam reads aloud + discusses what to look for. Safe: plans, does not spend.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Read the your-turn SKILL and its apply script. Then pick one of your own reels — or a synthetic beat sheet fixture — and ask Claude to draft a drafts dot j-son entry for it. First surface the reel's own material — the source chapter, the body beats' narration text — and draft one prompt a curious viewer would paste after watching. Then dry-run apply your turn against that draft and read the report before touching a real reel.

props.segment: Draft a drafts.json entry for one reel
props.command: Read skills/make/your-turn/SKILL.md and skills/make/your-turn/scripts/apply_your_turn.py in full. Then pick ONE reel of your own — or the synthetic beat sheet fixture in youtube/brutalist/claude-liam-brutalist-skill-your-turn/demo/. First surface the reel's own material (metadata.source, the body beats' narration_text) and draft ONE drafts.json entry for it: a prompt 3-5 sentences long, first person, ending in a concrete multi-part ask that goes one step DEEPER than the video. Then dry-run apply_your_turn.py against that draft and read the report before touching any real reel.
